To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capacity to activate persisting tick-born encephalitis virus was shown for kefzol (cefamycin) and ristomycine.
the capacity of wide-spectum antibiotics to activate the persistant tick-borne encepalitis virus and to cause exacerbation of chronic TBE was investigated in hamsters.

In the course of the study, we found that the capacity of wide-specturm antibiotics to activate the persistant tick-borne encepalitis virus and cause exacerbation of chronic TBE process in Syrian hamsters is determined by their ability to inhibit the activity of ribonuclease and to induce the synthesis of interferon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of choice of antibiotics for treatment of bacterial infections concomitants with tick-borne encepalitis.
a new aspect of antibiotic therapy in patients with TBE, namely, a possibility for the antibiotic to activate a persistent virus.
the development of a strategy for choosing antibiotics for therapy of secondary infections associated with chronic TBE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibiotic of choice for treatment of bacterial infections associated with TBE should be one of those that do not activate persisting virus, or at most, only weakly activate it.
the antibiotic treatment of TBE-associated bacterial infections should be performed using antibiotics devoid of provoking effect.
antibiotics should be used in TBE patients only when indicated, and then the least potent activators of persistent TBE virus should be preferred.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the choice of antibiotics for treating secondary bacterial infections associated with TBE should be based not only on their antibacterial activity but also on their capacity to activate or inactivate the persisting virus.
antibiotics devoid of evident provocation of persisting TVE virus and immunodepression (penicillin, ampidillin, levomycetins) are the best drugs for therapy of bacterial infections in TBE.
the antibiotic of choice for treatment of TBE-associated secondary infections is levoridan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotics should not be administered in the acute period of TBE.
the antibiotic therapy for TBE should be carried out only in the absence of signs of secondary bacterial infection or with the use of drugs devoid of evident provocative effect.
antibiotics with a high degree of activation of the persisting tick borne encephalitis virus should be avoided in patients with TBE.
